title: Introduction to anatomy and physiology
summaryMarkdown:
## What you learn in this chapter

Anatomy describes the structure of the body; physiology explains its functions. For admission, you must recognize the planes and sections of the body, directional terms, and the organization from cell to organ.

## Key concepts

- **Anatomy** vs **physiology**: form and function are complementary.
- **Planes and sections**: sagittal, frontal (coronal), transverse (horizontal).
- **Directional terms**: superior/inferior, anterior/posterior, medial/lateral, proximal/distal.
- **Levels of organization**: chemical → cellular → tissue → organ → system → organism.
- **Homeostasis**: maintaining internal parameters within normal limits through feedback.

## Clinical and exam connections

- Mistakes in planes/sections lead to misinterpretations of images (X-ray, CT).
- Directional terms are used in describing injuries and procedures.

## Common exam pitfalls

- Confusion between **proximal/distal** (applies to limbs, not to the axis) vs **superior/inferior**.
- Mixing up the sagittal and coronal planes in simple drawings.

## Mini-summary

This chapter introduces the language of anatomy and physiology: planes, sections, spatial orientation, and structural hierarchy. Homeostasis connects structure to adaptive function. Master the directional terms—they appear in all subsequent modules.
